activity_context.topic_title: Finding the First Term of an Arithmetic Series

feedback.problem: What is the first term of an arithmetic series if the common difference is $d=0.6,$ and the sum of the first $37$ terms is ${S}_{37}=444?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given the common difference of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=37$, $d=0.6$, and ${S}_{N}=444$ into the formula above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}444 & =\frac{37}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(37-1)(0.6)) \\ 888 & =37(2{a}_{1}+21.6) \\ \frac{888}{37} & =2{a}_{1}+21.6 \\ 2.4 & =2{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =1.2.\end{aligned}
$$
